text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager — routing-anomaly: elevated 5xx rate for requests originating APAC -> eu-west-1. Severity: P1. Runbook: cross-region-routing. Pager: @oncall-net
Jesse: seeing spikes in 502/504 from eu-west1 when requests originate ap-southeast-1. Grafana dashboard shows a step increase at 10:02 UTC.
Mina: confirmed. Latency also up ~200ms for affected buckets. Looks correlated with a routing-policy rollout that started at 09:58 UTC.
Patrick: pinging the deploy logs — deploying routing-policy v3.2 to control-plane at 09:59:12. Might be rollout related.
Anika: customers reporting degraded responses. Support thread: ticket #43218 mentions timeouts and retries, priority customers impacted: 3 enterprise tenants, several PLG flows.
dns-eng: seeing a small surge of NXDOMAINs from eu-west1 health probes to apac edge. Could be unrelated but worth checking.
Jesse: quick check: `redwoodctl routing get --policy active --regions ap-southeast-1,eu-west-1` shows inconsistent pin metadata: some prefixes still pinned to eu-west-1, others flipped to eu-central-1 unexpectedly.
Mina: that matches request traces — some sessions are being steered to eu-central for models that should be served from eu-west. When we steer across regions requests sometimes timeout due to thermal limits on fallback nodes.
Patrick: can we roll back the routing-policy rollout? What's the risk to ongoing traffic?
Jesse: rollback is available. `redwoodctl rollout rollback routing-policy v3.2 --to v3.1` will revert control-plane decisions. I can queue it but need approval for immediate rollback.
Anika: recommend rollback. Customer-impact >5% for APAC-origin requests to EU models. Support ops wants a short blurb for affected customers.
support-ops: please include expected ETA and mitigation steps in the blurb: we've advised retry/backoff but customers need guaranteed routing.
Jesse: initiating rollback now. Command run: ```
# rollback routing policy
redwoodctl rollout rollback routing-policy v3.2 --to v3.1 --force
```
incident-bot: Rollback initiated by Jesse at 10:12:34 UTC. Estimated completion 2m.
Mina: I'm watching the control-plane logs. Getting a flurry of `policy-eval: region-mismatch` warnings for prefixes that have cached pins in edge proxies. Need to flush pin cache in apac edge.
dns-eng: cache flush for edge pin metadata is rolling; command: `edgectl cache flush --type pin --region ap-southeast-1 --prefixes 7/8` — running now.
Patrick: also turning on a temporary steering override to prefer local region for APAC-origin traffic: `redwoodctl route override --region ap-southeast-1 --prefer local --ttl 30s` to reduce cross-region fallbacks during the cache propagate window.
Anika: support-ops, short blurb for customers: "We detected an anomaly in cross-region routing after a recent policy rollout affecting APAC->EU traffic. We've rolled back the policy and applied temporary overrides; you may see intermittent errors for up to 5 minutes. We're monitoring — will update when stable."
support-ops: posting that now in affected tickets and updating status page.
Jesse: rollback finished at 10:15:02 UTC. Control plane reports policy version v3.1 active across regions.
Mina: metrics trending back to baseline but there are still tails. I'm seeing 2xx recovery for most paths but a minority of sessions still get timeouts — likely edge pin cache TTL.
dns-eng: edge pin cache TTLs were at 5m. We flushed; new pins should re-evaluate within TTL window. We also pushed a targeted pin-expire for prefixes showing mismatch: `edgectl pin expire --prefixes 10.64.0.0/12`.
Jesse: re-running probes: `redwoodctl probe run --from ap-southeast-1 --to eu-west-1 --count 200` — success rate 98% now, latency normalized for majority.
Anika: impact summary for post-incident notes: start 10:02 UTC, root cause: routing-policy rollout introduced a policy evaluation ordering bug causing stale pin metadata to be favored for a subset of prefixes; consequence: cross-region misrouting to eu-central and timeouts. Mitigation: rollback to v3.1, edge pin cache flush, temporary steering override, targeted pin-expires.
Patrick: action items: 1) postmortem to include reproducer and unit tests for evaluation ordering; 2) add a rollout canary monitor for cross-region latency delta; 3) reduce default edge pin TTL from 5m to 90s for faster recovery during rollouts or implement pin invalidation hook.
Mina: also recommend a health-check gating step in rollout pipeline: if cross-region 5xx rate increases >0.5% during canary, auto-pause.
support-ops: customers notified. Two enterprise accounts escalated to SEs — assigned.
incident-bot: Incident resolved -> mitigation applied. Severity downgraded to P2 at 10:28:40 UTC. Please add postmortem label and assign to oncall owners.
Jesse: final status: control plane on v3.1, steering override removed at 10:26 UTC after metrics stable, edge pin caches converged by 10:29 UTC. Closing on-call shift in 30m; handing to next oncall for postmortem follow-up.
on-call note from oncall-net: I'll own the follow-up and coordinate the postmortem, assigning Mina and Jesse as contributors.
Anika: thanks team. Quick debrief in #eng-runtime in 15 to capture notes. :thumbsup:
Patrick: logging runbook updates now.
support-ops: final customer update posted: ETA for full recovery confirmed.
Jesse: marking incident for follow-up ticket: INC-4982.
Anika: handing off to next oncall at 10:30 UTC — good job everyone."
